newsitem.title: USA: New York City garden dedicated to Katharine Hepburn.
newsitem.headline: New York City garden dedicated to Katharine Hepburn.

text.p: A New York City garden was dedicated to film great Katharine Hepburn on Monday, her 90th birthday.
"Miss H," as director Anthony Harvey called her, remained at her home in Fenwick, Connecticut, overlooking the Long Island Sound, planners of the event said.
Harvey said Hepburn was doing well when he spoke to her over the weekend. When he remarked on her birthday, "She said, 'Don't mention it.' She hates birthdays," he said.
Hepburn was most likely celebrating by eating chocolates, "her most favourite thing," said Harvey, who directed her in her Academy Award-winning role in "The Lion in Winter."
Family members say she is frail, withdrawn and suffering from memory loss.

Hepburn lived in the Turtle Bay neighbourhood of New York City, where the garden is located, for six decades. The Katharine Hepburn Garden is part of the larger Dag Hammarskjold Plaza at the front of the United Nations.
Other Hollywood figures on hand for the occasion included director and writer Garson Kanin, who wrote such Hepburn films as "Adam's Rib" and "Pat and Mike," and actor Sam Waterston.
Hepburn won a record four Academy Awards for Best Actress, and her sophisticated, emancipated style has inspired generations of women.
